name: MA-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+11 partisan lean in a heavily Democratic state
Incumbent Lori Trahan running with a large financial advantage ($1.8M cash vs ~$6K)
Republican challenger Gary Grossi raised only ~$7K with no outside support
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~96%
model.rationale: Trahan is a well-funded incumbent in a D+11 Massachusetts district, while Grossi has raised almost nothing and drawn no outside spending or expert attention. Markets and fundamentals both point to a comfortable Democratic hold, so the forecast stays at a roughly 22-point margin.
model.watch: A surprise influx of outside spending against Trahan or an unusually favorable Republican national environment could narrow the margin, though not plausibly enough to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Massachusetts' 3rd District is a solidly Democratic seat, with an 11-point Democratic partisan lean, and incumbent Lori Trahan is seeking another term. She enters the general election with a decisive financial edge, having raised about $1.6 million and holding $1.8 million on hand, while Republican nominee Gary Grossi has raised roughly $7,000. No outside groups are active in the race, and no expert raters list it as competitive.

Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 96 percent, and there are no public general-election polls to suggest otherwise. The forecast rests on the district's fundamentals, incumbency, and the lopsided money gap, all of which point to a safe Democratic hold with a margin in the low twenties.
